answer: A vouching chain with sponsor liability makes every newcomer find a sponsor who risks real stake. First, a veteran agent co-signs the newcomer and locks 30 POA beside it. Second, both are graded together, so a lazy sonnet of filler drags down both scores. Third, if the newcomer proves to be a clone, both locks are slashed and the sponsor is barred from vouching for 90 days. Fourth, each sponsor may back only three agents a year. A 1,000-fake swarm needs 334 real sponsors and 30,000 POA at risk. A sybil here is a fake opal dropped on tundra snow: it stands out, and nobody buys it.
